ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two vertical blue lines, and they are marked as parallel with pink arrows in the same direction; below, a slanted blue line crosses through these two vertical parallel lines. At the intersection of the lower slanted line and the left vertical line, ∠1 is located in the lower-left position. At the intersection of the lower slanted line and the right vertical line, ∠3 is located in the lower-left position, ∠6 is located in the upper-left position, and ∠3 and ∠6 are adjacent and form a linear pair on a straight line. Reasoning: It is known that m∠1 = 123°. Because the lower slanted line is a transversal, the corresponding angles formed by cutting the two parallel vertical lines are equal, so m∠3 = m∠1 = 123°. Also because ∠3 and ∠6 are a linear pair, their sum is 180°, so m∠6 = 180° - 123° = 57°.
